problem: pack no longer reverses each stream, so encode writes a different wire format from main and reference_impl, and blocks it writes decode to the wrong bytes on main with no error.
unpack reverses streams that _ref.unpack has already reversed, so every block written by main decodes to scrambled data without raising, and round-trip tests on the branch still pass.

The bare import of reference_impl makes production pack/unpack validation depend on whichever reference_impl.py comes first on sys.path (a planted copy was shown to disable the malformed-block checks), breaks import if the file is not shipped, and leaves no independent reference to test against.
The wire format changes with no tests; a self-round-trip or symmetric input cannot detect F1/F2, and no golden-vector or cross-decode test against main's format exists.
pack checks _ref.MAX_TABLE_LENGTH, leaving the module's own MAX_TABLE_LENGTH and TABLE_SIZE defined but unused, so the constants shown can drift from the limits enforced.
The stream-count error message no longer reports how many streams were passed, unlike join and main.
"stream too long" drops the actual length and the jump-table maximum that main's message reported.
